raw_policy_excerpt:
# Ground rules
1. Respect our users' privacy. We oppose and condemn the actions of hackers who use vulnerability testing as an excuse, for example: exploiting vulnerabilities to steal user data, intrusion into Deriv's services, changing, copying, or stealing data from related system services.
2. Do not cause more harm than good.
3. Please provide detailed reports with reproducible steps.
4. Do not mass create accounts.
5. Only interact with accounts you own or with the explicit permission of the account holder.
6. Do not incur loss of funds that are not your own.
7. No destructive automated testing. Under no circumstance should automated testing cause intentional damage to our systems.
8. Do not publicly disclose vulnerabilities without our explicit consent.
9. Social engineering (e.g., phishing, vishing, smishing) is prohibited.
12. The final assessment of each vulnerability is determined by the impact, risk, and current mitigation measures.
15. Regarding any 0-day vulnerabilities, we will only accept the report if it has been > 30 days since the relevant patch release.
16. Vulnerabilities regarding information disclosure of cloud storage buckets (e.g., S3, KSS, FDS): We will confirm internally whether the information or link should be publicly accessible/viewable.

# Test plan
1. Include HTTP header 'X-HackerOne-Research: [H1 username]' in every testing request.
2. Use [username]@wearehackerone.com email alias for any accounts created.

# Bounty table (Important / General / Edge business)
CRITICAL: $5,000 / $2,000 / $1,500
HIGH: $2,500 / $1,500 / $500
MEDIUM: $500 / $250 / $100
LOW: $100 / $50 / $50

# Safe harbour
Any activities conducted in a manner consistent with this policy will be considered authorised conduct, and we will not initiate legal action against you. https://hackerone.com/deriv/safe_harbor

# Out of scope (web): Issues in 3rd party app myaffiliates; 3rd party support chatbox (Livechat/freshworks); Clickjacking without impact; XMLRPC brute-force/enumeration/DDoS; Firebase DB open without sensitive info; Design flaws; Self XSS; Theoretical subdomain takeovers; Session not invalidated after logout; DNS issues (MX, SPF); Missing security headers without direct vulnerability; and more.
